title: Vision Paper: Why Distributed LLM Post-Training and Decentralized Alignment Are Now Essential
abstract: arXiv:2611.05841v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This vision paper argues that distributed learning, including federated and decentralized, should become a first-class paradigm in LLM post-training, not merely a privacy add-on. Current methods like RLHF and DPO rest on an invisible assumption: preference data should be centralized. We contend this assumption is scientifically unjustified, practically unsustainable, and ethically problematic. As LLMs deploy into healthcare, law, finance, and multilingual communities, preference data originates from populations that cannot or will not centralize. We develop a three-pillar argument grounded in (1) privacy and data sovereignty, (2) pluralism and representational equity, and (3) robustness and scalability. We formalize key technical challenges unique to this intersection, reference drift, preference heterogeneity, and the DP-utility trade-off for contrastive losses, and propose concrete algorithmic directions, and sketch a research agenda.

translated_title: 愿景论文：为什么分布式LLM后训练与去中心化对齐如今至关重要
translated_abstract: 这篇愿景论文认为，分布式学习（包括联邦学习和去中心化学习）应成为LLM后训练中的一等范式，而不仅仅是隐私保护的附加功能。当前的RLHF和DPO等方法建立在一个隐含假设之上：偏好数据应当被集中化。我们认为这一假设在科学上站不住脚，在实践中不可持续，在伦理上也存在问题。随着LLM被部署到医疗、法律、金融和多语言社区，偏好数据来自无法或不愿将数据集中化的人群。我们构建了一个基于三大支柱的论证：(1) 隐私与数据主权，(2) 多元主义与表征公平，(3) 鲁棒性与可扩展性。我们形式化了这一交叉领域特有的关键技术挑战——参考漂移、偏好异质性以及对比损失的差分隐私-效用权衡，提出了具体的算法方向，并勾勒出一份研究议程。
tldr: 本文主张分布式学习应成为LLM后训练的一等范式，论证RLHF/DPO所依赖的偏好数据集中化假设不成立，并基于隐私主权、多元公平和鲁棒可扩展性三大支柱提出去中心化对齐的关键技术挑战与研究议程。
en_tdlr: This vision paper argues that distributed learning should become a first-class paradigm in LLM post-training, contending that the centralization assumption behind RLHF/DPO is scientifically unjustified and laying out a three-pillar research agenda for decentralized alignment covering privacy sovereignty, pluralism, and robustness.
